title: I started learning Godot in my late 50s and shipped my first game about six weeks later. AI made it possible.
author: annacrowgames
selftext:
I started learning Godot in mid-July. I had never made a game before, and about six weeks later I had my first game approved for the App Store.

It’s a hidden-object/history game called Anna Crow: Hidden Histories. Each case puts you in a historical scene and asks you to find things that don’t belong in that time period.

I don't believe I could have made it without AI. I used ChatGPT a lot while learning Godot. Not to generate the whole game and hand it to me, but more like having somebody sitting beside me who could explain why something wasn’t working or help me write or fix a script. I still had to build the scenes, wire everything together, test it, break it, and fix it again.

I used AI for most of the artwork too, and that turned out to be a much bigger job than I expected. Getting a beautiful image is relatively easy. Getting one that can survive being examined closely as a puzzle is not.

Hands are wrong. Objects melt together. Architecture makes no sense. Accidental errors are liberally spread throughout the scene. I spend far more time repairing an image in Photoshop than I spent generating it in the first place. And because the whole premise is finding anachronisms, I have to research everything else in the picture to make sure I haven’t accidentally created an anachronism I didn’t intend.

That has probably been the biggest surprise for me. AI didn’t eliminate the work. It let me attempt something that was previously beyond my abilities and then moved the difficult part somewhere else. I’m excited to see where it can help me go in the future. I’d be interested to hear from other people making games with AI. Has it actually saved you work, or mostly changed the kind of work you have to do?

comments.author: klas-klattermus
comments.body:
Congratulations on shipping a game! Hope you'll find lots of happiness and fulfillment from the creative endeavor of gamedev!

Oh its been huge, my problem has never really been doing the things but rather finding the time to do the thing. And AI sure streamlines a lot.

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: Thanks! And yeah, streamlining is a good way to put it. I’m finding AI doesn’t necessarily mean less work, but I can get through the stuff that used to slow me down a lot faster.

comments.author: Patera-Milenko
comments.body: I'm just starting this journey myself and having been using Ai to help me in the same fashion. It's been great having help, hard to trust sometimes but generally fantastic!

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: That sounds very familiar! The trust part is definitely something I’ve learned the hard way. It can be incredibly helpful or completely wrong with equal confidence. 😂

replies.author: Patera-Milenko
replies.body:
They are all so confident sounding sometimes. I'm just suss anymore and test my answers and questions across a couple to help correlate a semi reasonable answer lol Jokes it's really great to use but I do actually like to test them across a few. 

Paranoid but it seems to work lol

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: I do the same thing sometimes! I’ve learned that asking the same question a slightly different way can be pretty revealing too. Sometimes the second answer makes me realize I shouldn’t have trusted the first one at all.

replies.author: Patera-Milenko
replies.body: Totally true too, I find with me I'm not asking the "right" question more often than I like lol

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: Ooof, I feel that. And the occasional little mistakes on my end that change the nature of the question/answer don't help either.

replies.author: Patera-Milenko
replies.body: Totally true too, I find with me I'm not asking the "right" question more often than I like lol

comments.author: Left-Excitement3829
comments.body: That’s exactly what I tried explaining to a friend who is antiai games.  Without AI all of my stuff would never get made. A lot of others are the same , removing ai means removing access , I’m not going to learn 3d coding and c++ to make a silly side project.

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: Exactly. There are things I could probably learn to do eventually, but realistically I’m never going to have enough time to get good at all of them. AI lets me spend that time actually making the thing I want to make.

replies.author: Ianxcala
replies.body: I feel exactly the same. A lot of creative ideas were trapped, and how can come to life, which is great.

comments.author: pickleunicorn
comments.body:
Yes, AI does not solve anything magically. It's quicker than a human, but with the experience of an intern. I'm a developer myself and I love vibe coding things to test a proof of concept, but I know that at some point I will need to look at the code and make the AI refactor everything to make the project viable and maintainable in the long term. And that's really long. Also AI makes mistakes all the time and drifts as the window context grows. People thinking that AI is like pushing a button do not know what they're talking about.

Of course you can use AI like that, but this what's called slop.

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: The idea of refactoring everything to make the project viable and sustainable really resonates with me. It’s not easy, but I’ve received a lot of good feedback along the way and incorporated a lot of it into how the project is structured now.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: Seriously, good for you to have chosen to learn with the AI instead of giving everything to it. It's not the easiest but it's more rewarding, and you learn many things on the way.

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: Thanks! That’s really what I’ve tried to do. I don’t just want to make the game. I want to understand how I made it and how I can improve the process.

replies.author: pickleunicorn
replies.body: A true programmer in the heart

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: Congratulations! I'm 45 and although I had coding knowledge before I never got around developing a game. Now I have a published game and I'm about to ship another.

replies.author: annacrowgames
replies.body: That's awesome! I'm working on my second game as well. I really enjoy it.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: AI has helped me "unstuck" a million projects that where linked to something I couldn't figure out on my own.

comments.author: TAKAsFactory
comments.body:
Using AI allows you to create a "working prototype" incredibly quickly.  
But that is just the starting point of game development. It is the process of gradually refining various elements, injecting originality, and figuring out how to make the game fun, satisfying, and engaging—it is this accumulation of effort that creates a great game.  
AI will stick with you through that painstaking work—whether it takes hours, happens in the middle of the night, or involves tens of thousands of iterations. That is AI's greatest advantage.
